Posted September 8, 2008 

Analysis by Richard Cowan  

 

An article in yesterdays LA Times, Suicides up after warning, study shows, had nothing in it about cannabis, but should offer some insight into the debate on the psychiatric risks  or benefits  in teen cannabis use.   

Excerpts: "A 22% drop in prescriptions for antidepressants for teens and children following government warnings about hazards of the drugs led to a sharp increase in suicides the following year according to a report in the September issue of the American Journal of Psychiatry. 

 

In the year after the change in labeling, the suicide rate rose 14% among those younger than 19, the largest increase since the government started collecting suicide statistics in 1979 

 

A similar drop in prescriptions in the Netherlands led to a 49% increase in youth suicides over a two-year period, the team reported. They estimated that every 20% drop in antidepressant use among all ages in the U.S. would lead to a nearly 10% increase in suicides, an additional 3,040 deaths per year 

(MarijuanaNews note: The Dutch suicide rate was less than half the US rate prior to these warnings. For a comparison of international rates among young males, seehttp://www.nationmaster.com/graph/hea_sui_rat_you_mal-health-suicide-rate-young-males.)
  
 

In 2003 and 2004, the Food and Drug Administration mandated the black-box warning on them after research indicated that youths who took the drugs had an increase in suicidal thinking. The warning applied to patients younger than 19. 

 

Earlier this year, the warning was changed to include adults younger than 25. Many experts had argued against such warnings, contending that it would cause many patients to abandon treatment that they desperately needed. At least 3 million Americans now do not receive any treatment for their depression.

In 2003 and 2004, the Food and Drug Administration mandated the black-box warning on them after research indicated that youths who took the drugs had an increase in suicidal thinking. The warning applied to patients younger than 19. 

 

Earlier this year, the warning was changed to include adults younger than 25. Many experts had argued against such warnings, contending that it would cause many patients to abandon treatment that they desperately needed. At least 3 million Americans now do not receive any treatment for their depression. 

Well, as Michael Vick might say, I dont have a dog in this fight. It is off-topic for MarijuanaNews.com, but as I have previously noted, most of the American Columbine type shooters were using such drugs, and clearly the drugs do not work for everyone. 

See 

What If the Colorado Shooter Had Been Using Marijuana Instead Of A Pharmaceutical? Two Different Standards.   

and 

Ricky Williams and Our Paxil Problem. The Media Miss the Point, As Usual. "

What this latest research does tell us that is relevant for MarijuanaNews.com is that the medical profession does not really know whether widely used, FDA approved drugs help or hurt some young patients. Of course, they are even less able to know whether they may help some and hurt others. 

 

On the other hand, in the UK one finds much certainty that cannabis causes psychosis in teens who use cannabis. A recent article in the supposedly progressive New Statesman, An epidemic of cannabis use? by Dr Raj Persaud, the Gresham Professor for Public Understanding of Psychiatry and Consultant Psychiatrist at The MaudsleyHospital in South London, is illustrative.  

Excerpt: 

An enigma which frequently clouds the cannabis debate is - if its as dangerous as doctors and scientists claim - how come despite being possibly the most used illicit drug worldwide, the ill effects appear to affect so few?  

 

For example surveys suggest that as many as one in four of those aged from the late teens to the early twenties in the UK admit to having smoked cannabis recently  yet the rate of schizophrenia remains relatively but stubbornly low in comparison  roughly one in a hundred. 

(MarijuanaNews note: "Stubbornly low"? It must be frustrating that the facts don't support his premise.)

 

Professor Robin Murray, from the Institute of Psychiatry, has recently attempted to simplify the statistics. In the most recent comprehensive review of the research he estimates that the elimination of cannabis use in the UK would reduce the incidence of schizophrenia by approximately 8 per cent 

See 

UK Reefer Madness Spreads To Canada As Both Countries Move Toward Phoney Decrim Bills. One Cannabis User Dies of An Overdose, Another Commits Murder.  

(MarijuanaNews note: Even if cannabis were the proximate cause of schizophrenia in these cases, which is very far from proven, this statement is both arrogant and ignorant. Those who are so vulnerable might evntually have serious mental problems even if they never used cannabis. Of course, one might argue that the elimination of alcohol, or fatty foods, or sex outside of marriage, or driving while fatigued [the largest cause of accidents], etc. might prevent all sorts of problems, but so might eliminating psychiatry. Of course, there might be costs and unintended consequences, but it would be such a perfect world!) 

 

He concludes: 

 

I just wish it was possible for more to experience my own ward at the Bethlem Royal and Maudsley NHS Hospitals Trust where cannabis abuse appears an epidemic and has lit a fuse the explosion from which, in the form of possibly dramatic higher rates of schizophrenia in the near future, could have massive fall out  affecting us all. 

 

A comment posted on the NewStatesman site, says something about the diagnosis of cannabis psychosis: 

 

A friend of mine smoked cannabis for years, he had a short period of psychosis and was admitted to hospital. He had moved to a new town to follow his wife to her new job. He could not get work, their relationship deteriorated and became marked by constant arguments and stress. When he was admitted to hospital his wife said it was due to cannabis and said nothing of the other problems. It was duly noted as a case of cannabis psychosis. After 2 weeks he discharged himself, left his wife, got a job and continued to smoke cannabis. That was fifteen years ago. On record he is a case of cannabis psychosis but his problems seemed more related to his social situation. Fifteen years later still smoking cannabis and having a happy life he has never had any hint of psychosis again. When we consider the impecise nature of psychiatric diagnosis, the fact tha many families find cannabis psychosis a more acceptable explanation than other possible explanations, one wonders how many recorded cases of cannabis psychosis have any real scientific basis.

For example surveys suggest that as many as one in four of those aged from the late teens to the early twenties in the UK admit to having smoked cannabis recently  yet the rate of schizophrenia remains relatively but stubbornly low in comparison  roughly one in a hundred. 

(MarijuanaNews note: "Stubbornly low"? It must be frustrating that the facts don't support his premise.)

 

Several articles have dealt with the UK reefer madness. I recommend 

The Politics of Schizophrenia By FRED GARDNER 

and 

 Bad science: Cannabis data comes to the crunch by Ben Goldacre in The Guardian  

All of this brings me back to my original point. It is entirely possible that, like anti-depressants, cannabis may help some people with mental problems and harm others, but establishment psychiatry shows no interest in its possible benefits, and unlike the anti-depressants, which are huge products for Big Pharma, there is no way to find out.  

 

Moreover, cannabis is not just one thing. It is a plant with a variety of active ingredients, the ratios of which vary from strain to strain. Prohibition makes it much more difficult to know which strain does what, and certainly people with mental problems would have a very hard time knowing which is which, even in Holland.  

See

"Cannabis May Help Combat Schizophrenia"  

Or "Marijuana-Like Chemical Found In Schizophrenics"  

 Is Schizophrenia A Journalistic Disorder? -- 2 Articles  

 

In fairness to the medical profession, it should be recognized that prohibition does make it very difficult to study cannabis. The DEA controls access to cannabis and NIDA provides funding for over 80% of the research done on illegal drugs, and their agenda is to protect the drug war from science. 

See
How NIDA Made Monkeys of the Media. 4 Primates Are News; 4 Million People Are Not. Analysis by Richard Cowan
 

and 

 How the Prohibitionist Funding Racket Really Works Shown As Califano Shills for DEA and NIDA.

and 

New Media Merger: Washington Post Merges With NIDA.
and 

More Proof That The Drug War Is Really A War On Cannabis. Plus: Sabotaging Medical Cannabis Research And Lying About It. Analysis by Richard Cowan  

 

However, there is one area where psychiatry, especially in the UK, but really everywhere, is guilty of malpractice on a huge scale.  

 

The psychiatric establishment either advocates or tolerates the use of state violence against cannabis users, and yet I cannot find anywhere a study on  or even concern about the psychological impact on cannabis users of being arrested and jailed for the use of cannabis.  

 

Moreover, if cannabis use really does have adverse affects on the mental health of some users, especially the young, dont we have an even greater reason to protect them from the trauma of the criminal justice system?  

 

If they are arrested for a real crime, it may be unavoidable, but the notion of prophylactic state violence ostensibly to prevent some possible adverse affects of cannabis is malpractice on an unimaginable scale. 

 

In the real world psychiatry is being used to justify massive state violence, especially against the young, and yet, blinded by the prohibitionist paradigm, they pretend that it does not exist.  

See 

The Theory and Practice of Chaos  Analysis By Richard Cowan  

and

Conference On Rehab Racketeers Tied To Bush Will Raise Important Issues: Saving Children From Drug Treatment Abuse. Saving DEAland from Drug War Lite. A Conference That Should Embarrass Washington.

and 

Calling All Quacks: The Therapeutic Police State and the Politicization of Medicine. Doctors Cannot Study The Violence of Cannabis Prohibition. Because They Are The Disease, Not The Cure.  

and 

If The Best Two Word Explanation for Cannabis Prohibition Is Bad Journalism, The Best 3 Word Explanation Is Quack, Quack, Quack. -- Wholesale Malpractice In UK As Lambeth Experiment Spreads.  

 

 

Second, I have often observed that arrogance and ignorance are found together so often that it is easy to assume cause and effect, but it is not unique to psychiatry. 

 

In both DEAland and Canada there are large numbers of people using cannabis for a very wide range of ailments, but the medical establishment has shown no interest in studying them, while still claiming that we need more research. (There are people doing the same in many other counties, but it would be more difficult to study them.) 

See 

Live Free or Die  In Pain. The Ignorance and Arrogance of the Quacks Who Deny Pain Relief to the Sick and Dying.
